longTitle.officialTitle: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to modernize the integrated public alert and warning system of the United States, and for other purposes.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Modernization Act of 2015”.

section.heading: INTEGRATED PUBLIC ALERT AND WARNING SYSTEM MODERNIZATION.

subsection.heading: In general.—
Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Subcommittee.—

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (in this subsection referred to as the “Administrator”) shall establish a subcommittee to the National Advisory Council established under section 508 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 318) to be known as the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Subcommittee (in this subsection referred to as the “Subcommittee”).

paragraph.heading: Membership.—
paragraph.chapeau: Notwithstanding section 508(c) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 318(c)), the Subcommittee shall be composed of the following members (or their designees):

subparagraph.content: The Deputy Administrator for Protection and National Preparedness of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
The Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission.
The Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the Department of Commerce.
The Assistant Secretary for Communications and Information of the Department of Commerce.
The Under Secretary for Science and Technology of the Department of Homeland Security.
The Under Secretary for the National Protection and Programs Directorate.
The Director of Disability Integration and Coordination of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
The Chairperson of the National Council on Disability.

subparagraph.chapeau: Qualified individuals appointed by the Administrator as soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act from among the following:

clause.content: Representatives of State and local governments, representatives of emergency management agencies, and representatives of emergency response providers.
Representatives from federally recognized Indian tribes and national Indian organizations.

clause.chapeau: Individuals who have the requisite technical knowledge and expertise to serve on the Subcommittee, including representatives of—

subclause.content: vendors, developers, and manufacturers of systems, facilities, equipment, and capabilities for the provision of communications services;
the broadcasting industry, including public broadcasting;
the commercial mobile radio service industry;
national organizations representing individuals with disabilities, the blind, deaf, and hearing-loss communities, individuals with access and functional needs, and the elderly;
organizations representing individuals with limited-English proficiency.

clause.content: Qualified representatives of such other stakeholders and interested and affected parties as the Administrator considers appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Chairperson.—
paragraph.content: The Deputy Administrator for Protection and National Preparedness of the Federal Emergency Management Agency shall serve as the Chairperson of the Subcommittee.

subparagraph.heading: Initial meeting.—
subparagraph.content: The initial meeting of the Subcommittee shall take place not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: Other meetings.—
subparagraph.content: After the initial meeting, the Subcommittee shall meet, at least annually, at the call of the Chairperson.

paragraph.heading: Consultation with nonmembers.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Subcommittee and the program offices for the integrated public alert and warning system for the United States shall consult with individuals and entities that are not represented on the Subcommittee to consider new and developing technologies that may be beneficial to the public alert and warning system, including—

subparagraph.content: the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency;
entities engaged in federally funded research; and
academic institutions engaged in relevant work and research.
develop recommendations for an integrated public alert and warning system; and

subparagraph.chapeau: in developing the recommendations under subparagraph (A), consider—

clause.content: recommendations for common alerting and warning protocols, standards, terminology, and operating procedures for the public alert and warning system; and

clause.chapeau: recommendations to provide for a public alert and warning system that—

subclause.content: has the capability to adapt the distribution and content of communications on the basis of geographic location, risks, or personal user preferences, as appropriate;
has the capability to alert and warn individuals with disabilities and individuals with limited-English proficiency;
to the extent appropriate, incorporates multiple communications technologies;
is designed to adapt to, and incorporate, future technologies for communicating directly with the public;
is designed to provide alerts to the largest portion of the affected population feasible, including nonresident visitors and tourists, and improve the ability of remote areas to receive alerts;
promotes local and regional public and private partnerships to enhance community preparedness and response; and

provides redundant alert mechanisms, if practicable, to reach the greatest number of people regardless of whether they have access to, or use, any specific medium of communication or any particular device.

subparagraph.heading: Subcommittee submission.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Subcommittee shall submit to the National Advisory Council a report containing any recommendations required to be developed under paragraph (6) for approval by the National Advisory Council.

subparagraph.heading: Submission by national advisory council.—
subparagraph.chapeau: If the National Advisory Council approves the recommendations contained in the report submitted under subparagraph (A), the National Advisory Council shall submit the report to—

clause.content: the head of each agency represented on the Subcommittee;
the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate; and
the Committee on Homeland Security and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.

paragraph.heading: Termination.—
paragraph.content: The Subcommittee shall terminate not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this Act and the amendments made by this Act such sums as may be necessary for each of fiscal years 2016, 2017, and 2018.

paragraph.heading: Definition.—
paragraph.content: In this subsection, the term “participating commercial mobile service provider” has the meaning given that term under section 10.10(f) of title 47, Code of Federal Regulations, as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Limitations.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this Act, including an amendment made by this Act, shall be construed—

clause.content: of the Federal Communications Commission; or
provided under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq.);

subparagraph.content: to provide the Secretary of Homeland Security with authority to require any action by the Department of Commerce, the Federal Communications Commission, or any nongovernmental entity;
to apply to, or to provide the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency with authority over, any participating commercial mobile service provider;

to alter in any way the wireless emergency alerts service established under the Warning, Alert, and Response Network Act (47 U.S.C. 1201 et seq.) or any related orders issued by the Federal Communications Commission after October 13, 2006; or
to provide the Federal Emergency Management Agency with authority to require a State or local jurisdiction to use the integrated public alert and warning system of the United States.
